fire_1.attack: New live-runtime Rust probe (amphora-assurance-capabilities/tests/cf_packet_blueprint_citation_binding_probe.rs) builds a CroProtocolPackageV2 'final assembly' packet whose candidate_binding carries a blueprint_citations{path,sha256} entry, re-runs the T-02/W-CRO1 attack shape against it (0 regressions), then probes the NEW clause the done_criterion names: whether a cited blueprint sha256 that does not match the real blueprint.md file is caught.
fire_1.finding: CroProtocolPackageV2::validate()/sign()/verify_signature() ACCEPT a packet whose cited blueprint sha256 does not match the real blueprint.md file's bytes, ACCEPT a packet with no blueprint citation at all, and ACCEPT fabricated locked_numeric_thresholds values as long as protocol_lock_sha256 is self-derived from that map (never checked against any external source). protocol_lock_sha256 binds locked_numeric_thresholds to ITSELF only, never to a cited blueprint artifact's actual bytes -- there is no field or check anywhere in the compiled runtime implementing 'the packet citing every blueprint artifact by path+sha256 so the thresholds are content-bound to the blueprint they came from'.
fire_1.next_fire_should: Attempt the repair: add a blueprint-citation content-binding check to CroProtocolPackageV2::validate() (or a new packager-level assembly function) that (a) requires candidate_binding (or a dedicated field) to carry blueprint_citations entries with path+sha256 for every blueprint artifact locked_numeric_thresholds claims to derive from, and (b) verifies each cited sha256 against the real file's bytes at validate/sign time -- mirroring the computed_protocol_lock_sha256() pattern W-CRO1 used to repair T-02. Then re-run this exact probe (same harness sha256) as the acceptance test; CLAIM_SURVIVED only if all 3 new axis probes now fail closed AND the T-02/W-CRO1 shape still holds (0 regressions), with a positive control planting the same mismatched-hash defect and confirming detection.

fire_2.mode: rotation (not an assigned CF-PACKET campaign fire -- picked up as the strongest standing gap found during a rotation-mode fire against amphora-cro-protocol-packager)
fire_2.observation: Between fire_1 and this fire, a partial repair landed in amphora-assurance-capabilities/src/lib.rs (blueprint_citation_entries(), verify_blueprint_citations(root), and a validate()-level structural presence check for blueprint_citations when locked_numeric_thresholds is non-empty) plus an acceptance-test probe (amphora-assurance-capabilities/tests/cf_packet_repair_content_binding_probe.rs, authored 2026-08-11) -- but the probe was never run-and-signed into a receipt or logged to the falsification ledger, and the repair was never wired into sign()/verify_signature(): those two functions still call validate() only and never call verify_blueprint_citations(root).
fire_2.attack: Ran the existing, unmodified probe twice (two-replay, byte-identical). Confirmed: a packet whose blueprint_citations[0].sha256 does NOT match the real blueprint.md bytes still validate()s Ok, sign()s Ok, and verify_signature()s Ok against an honest TrustStore -- only the separate, non-mandatory verify_blueprint_citations(root) call (which sign()/verify_signature() never invoke) catches the mismatch.
fire_2.finding: The done_criterion clause is still not established by the packet's own DSSE Ed25519 signature. Structural presence of a citation is now enforced (fire_1's 'no citation at all' gap IS closed), but content MATCH against the real cited file is enforced only by a differently-shaped, filesystem-dependent function outside the sign/verify API -- easy for any caller who follows this module's normal sign()/verify_signature() pattern to omit.
fire_2.next_fire_should: Give verify_signature() (and/or sign()) an optional root: Option<&Path> parameter, or add a new wrapper (e.g. verify_signature_and_citations(root)) that also calls verify_blueprint_citations(root) whenever locked_numeric_thresholds is non-empty, so a fabricated blueprint citation cannot produce a validly-signed, independently-verifying packet. Re-run amphora-assurance-capabilities/tests/cf_packet_repair_content_binding_probe.rs (same harness sha256 e21878fea34bf1933beb3656ac4a6e2514b18279350f3914aadf0f7c60f531af) as the acceptance test; CLAIM_SURVIVED only if the wrong_blueprint_citation probe's sign_ok/verify_signature_ok both flip to false while the control (correct citation) and T-02/W-CRO1 shape probes keep passing.
